question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-5 & -2 & -3 \\ -1 & -6 & -3 \\ 5 & 10 & 11\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 8\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}-4 & a & -1 \\ 2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & b & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Given that $A=PD{P}^{-1},$ find the value of $\frac{a}{b}.$
question.worked_solution:
Notice that $D={P}^{-1}AP$ is a diagonalization of the matrix $A.$

From the diagonal matrix $D,$ we find that the eigenvalues of $A$ are

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}={\lambda }_{2}=-4\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}=8.$

The second column of $P$ corresponds to $\lambda =-4.$ Computing $A-\lambda I,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-4)I & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & -2 & -3 \\ -1 & -6 & -3 \\ 5 & 10 & 11\end{aligned}]-(-4)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & -3 \\ -1 & -2 & -3 \\ 5 & 10 & 15\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & -3 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & -3 & 0 \\ 5 & 10 & 15 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+5{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ are free variables. From the first equation we obtain 

$$
{x}_{1}=-2{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}.
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2},{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Comparing this with the second column of $P,$ we deduce that ${x}_{2}=0.$ Now, setting ${x}_{3}=1$ and substituting our values for ${x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ into the general solution, we obtain the following: 

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{b}=-\frac{3}{1}=-3.$
